encounters.cc: Patient presents with exertional chest discomfort described as dull, pressure-like sensation in the center of the chest occurring with stair climbing.

lines: Patient presents with exertional chest discomfort described as dull, pressure-like sensation in the center of the chest occurring with stair climbing.
The patient with diabetes returns for follow-up of prior chest discomfort.
He describes a dull, pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest that occurs after climbing stairs and resolves within a few minutes of rest.
- Erectile dysfunction (organic, secondary to diabetes mellitus) (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
His medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and metformin.
He does not smoke or drink alcohol.
Blood pressure of 138/84 mm Hg and heart rate of 72/min
A recent ECG shows nonspecific ST-T changes, and an exercise stress test is positive for inducible ischemia.
His physician starts him on a medication to reduce myocardial oxygen demand.
The patient is instructed to take the medication sublingually at the onset of symptoms and to remain seated afterward.
He reports rapid relief of chest discomfort within minutes of taking the pill.
On follow-up, the frequency and severity of anginal episodes have significantly improved.
The patient is advised not to use the medication concurrently with drugs for erectile dysfunction.
